title: Coherence vs Entrainment in Human-AI Agentic Systems: Agent-Based Model and Experiment Data
description: NetLogo agent-based model investigating how AI agent integration affects resilience in coordinated socio-technical systems. Distinguishes entrainment (phase-locking alignment) from coherence (identity-preserving coupling) and tests system behaviour across AI proportions, repeated stress, and mixed-regime populations. This version is the TENCON 2026 camera-ready deposit: every BehaviorSpace run is seeded by run number, so all reported statistics regenerate deterministically. Includes the seeded primary experiments H001–H003 (1,500 runs), the one-at-a-time robustness sweeps S-H004/S-H005 (20,000 runs), the fine-grained coherence-pole sweep S-H006 (1,400 runs), the unseeded March 2026 exports (exports/archive-pre-seed/) for comparison, the analysis scripts that print every paper number (notebooks/validate_baseline.py, paper_stats_seeded.py, sensitivity_analysis.py), and publication figures.
